sections.heading: Who we are
body: These terms are an agreement between you and Andrii Nalyvaiko, a sole proprietor in Lviv, Ukraine, who makes the I Love My Parents app ("the app", "we"). Contact: support@ilovemyparents.app.
By using the app you agree to these terms and to our privacy policy at ilovemyparents.app/privacy/. If you do not agree, please do not use the app.

sections.heading: What the app is, and what it is not
body: The app helps a family know that an older parent is OK each day: the parent taps "I am OK", gets pill reminders and can ask the family for help, and family members are told when a check-in does not come.

The app is not an emergency service, not a medical device and not a replacement for care, supervision or medical advice. It depends on phones, the internet, notifications and our servers, any of which can be late or fail. Never rely on the app alone for someone's safety. In an emergency, call 911 (999 in the UK) or your local emergency number.

sections.heading: Who can use it
body: You must be at least 18 years old to set up a family or join one as a family member. A parent may use the app when a family member has set it up for them, with their agreement.

When you add a parent or another person to your family, you confirm that they agree to be added and to share what the app shows the family. Keep the codes and invitation links you are given private: anyone who has one can join your family until it expires or is used.

sections.heading: Your account and your content
body: You are responsible for what you and your family put into the app, such as names, phone numbers, pill names and photos. Do not use the app to upload anything unlawful or anything you have no right to share.

You keep your content. You allow us to store it and show it to the members of your family only as needed to run the app, as described in the privacy policy. You can delete your account and data in the app at any time.

sections.heading: Plans, trials and payment
body: The daily check-in is free. Some features need the Family plan, a subscription paid monthly or yearly. Prices are shown in the app before you buy and may differ by country.

Subscriptions are sold and billed by Apple (App Store) or Google (Google Play), under their terms. A new Family plan may start with a free trial; if you do not cancel at least 24 hours before the trial ends, the subscription starts and you are charged.

A subscription renews automatically for the same period until you cancel it. Cancel in your App Store or Google Play account settings; deleting the app does not cancel it. When you cancel, the plan stays active until the end of the period you paid for. Refunds are handled by Apple or Google under their policies.
We may change prices for future periods. The store will tell you before a new price applies, and you can cancel before it does.

sections.heading: Fair use
body: Do not misuse the app: do not try to get into other families' data, break or overload our systems, copy or resell the app, or use it to harass or track anyone without their agreement. We may suspend or close an account that does this.

sections.heading: Changes and availability
body: We improve the app over time and may change, add or remove features. We try to keep it running at all times but cannot promise that it will always be available or free of errors.
If we change these terms in a way that matters, we will update the date at the top of this page. Using the app after that means you accept the new terms.

sections.heading: Liability
body: The app is provided "as is". To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for any harm or loss that comes from a notification, reminder or alert that was late, missed or not delivered, or from relying on the app instead of other care. Our total liability to you is limited to the amount you paid us for the app in the 12 months before the claim.
Nothing in these terms limits rights you have as a consumer that cannot be limited by law in your country.

body: These terms are governed by the laws of Ukraine, except where the consumer laws of your country say otherwise.
